presets.label: Meta Model API
presets.note: Pay-as-you-go Meta Model API. Get a key at https://dev.meta.ai (Meta calls it MODEL_API_KEY; export it here as META_MODEL_API_KEY) — a Meta developer account needs a payment method before it can serve requests, and every call is metered per token. A Muse Code subscription does NOT work here: Meta scopes that credential to the Muse Code CLI and bills any other key pay-as-you-go (dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/subscriptions). The Contributor tier (muse-spark-1.3-contributor) is cheap because Meta trains on your prompts — about 92% off input, 95% off output, 99% off cached input; do not send confidential material through it. Muse Wonder (muse-wonder-1.0, preview) is Standard mode only on this API ($4 input / $20 output per 1M tokens, no Contributor tier) and accepts reasoning effort up to max; the Spark rows stop at xhigh. Muse Spark is also reachable through resellers: command-code carries both tiers, opencode-go serves only muse-spark-1.3-contributor.

presets.label: opencode zen
presets.note: Keyed OpenCode Zen gateway. Free models on this tier are often short-window rate-limited at roughly 15-20 requests/minute (community-measured; OpenCode does not publish RPM). Zen may return generic 429s without Retry-After / X-RateLimit headers; when Retry-After is omitted, opencodex adds a synthetic backoff hint (upstream Retry-After still wins). Docs: https://opencode.ai/docs/zen/. Free-model prompts may be retained for training — do not send confidential material.

presets.label: Opper
presets.note: EU-hosted AI gateway: one OpenAI-compatible endpoint and one key in front of 30+ providers. Bare model ids are pools (claude-sonnet-4-6, gpt-5.5) and Opper picks the route per request; vendor/model ids (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6) pin one provider. The catalogue is discovered live from /v3/compat/models with your key; the public list is at opper.ai/models. Token rates are the model providers' rates with no markup; Opper charges a 3% fee when you buy credits.

presets.label: OpenGateway
presets.note: Sionic AI's OpenAI-compatible gateway. Public live discovery lists active models served on Chat Completions (plus pinned Responses-only rows), with Sionic-served ultrafast models first. The public catalog cannot validate keys.

presets.label: TokenLab
presets.note: OpenAI-compatible API gateway. Create a workspace API key at tokenlab.sh. Live discovery lists tool-capable chat models available to your key and delivery policy.

presets.label: Modelflare
presets.note: OpenAI-compatible relay for Claude, GPT, GLM and DeepSeek chat models. The original four seeded models were verified with chat, streaming and tool calls; GPT-6.1 Terra is a preemptive seed pending provider verification. deepseek-v4.1-flash is listed upstream but currently answers 503 and is left out. An ordinary key only reaches its own routing group's models; a Smart key reaches the verified seeded models. Image and video models are not served through this Chat preset. Upstream latency varies widely (a few seconds to about 30 s) with occasional transient 503s.

presets.label: AI Stupid Level
presets.note: Smart Router that sends each request to a model chosen from AI Stupid Level's benchmarks, using the provider keys saved on your AI Stupid Level account (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM), so each provider bills you directly with no markup. Routing modes: auto-coding (the default), auto-tooling, auto-reasoning, auto-best, plus value and speed modes. A real model id from the live list, such as claude-opus-5-5, pins one model. The X-AISM-Model response header names the model that answered. Text only.

presets.label: Xiaomi MiMo (OpenAI Chat)
presets.note: Official Xiaomi MiMo OpenAI-compatible Chat endpoint. V2.6 thinking is on/off: none disables it; high is the client-compatible on value, not a distinct reasoning strength. Older models retain their existing effort contract.

presets.label: Xiaomi MiMo (token plan)
presets.note: Xiaomi MiMo paid token plan. Pinned to the Chat wire: the Responses endpoint rejects freeform (custom) tools such as apply_patch with 400 responses_feature_not_supported, so agentic turns fail there while plain turns succeed. Reasoning tiers above high are clamped.
